finalText:
Redis crashed at 2:14 AM (connection refused to 10.0.0.12:6379), and the app couldn't recover.

When Redis went down, the cache layer fell back to hammering the database directly. Every cache miss became a database hit. The workload amplified — what should have been a few cache hits turned into hundreds of direct queries. The request queue overflowed from 52 to 568 requests (max is 500) in just 17 minutes. By 2:31 AM, the Node process ran out of heap memory trying to buffer the backlog, crashed with code 134, and supervisor killed the whole service.

The immediate fix is getting Redis back up on 10.0.0.12:6379. Once that reconnects, the cache layer should stabilize and the queue should drain. You might also want to add circuit-breaker logic or a lower cache-bypass timeout so the system fails faster instead of queuing infinitely when Redis is down.
